messages:
maria-dev: Quick check — onboarding aurora-13b-mqa. weights are at s3://redwood-models/aurora/13b/mqa/v1, but runtime fails at init with tokenizer/vocab mismatch error. Anyone seen this layout before?

tony-runtime: @maria-dev I can take a look. What error exactly? stack trace/log snippet helps. Also which runtime build are you on? (stable-2026-11 or nightly-canary)

maria-dev: paste from node logs: ```RuntimeError: tokenizer.vocab_size (50265) != model.config.vocab_size (50000)
During init of TokenizerWrapper -> EmbeddingMatrix``` — running stable-2026-11. No custom tokenizer files in the model tar besides tokenizer.json and merges.

ritesh-ml: That usually means the tokenizer was trained with extra special tokens we didn't ship in the model config. Check tokenizer.json for added tokens (like <|sentinel|> or multi-byte tokens). Also confirm we didn't accidentally use byte-level BPE vs our expected unicode BPE.

sara-se: quick grep shows tokenizer.json contains 265 extra entries labeled "<extra_\uXXXX>" — likely sentinel tokens for retrieval augmentation. Model config expects 50000; tokenizer has 50265. Two options: regenerate model config to match vocab size or provide a trimmed tokenizer mapping. Which is easier for this release?

maria-dev: prefer not to rebuild weights. Can we patch model config to accept vocab_size=50265? any backward compat risks?

tony-runtime: We support differing vocab sizes only if the embedding matrix matches. If model checkpoint's embedding shape is 50000, forcing config to 50265 will break. Check embedding.bin shape in the checkpoint shard. You can run: ```python tools/check_weights.py --path s3://redwood-models/aurora/13b/mqa/v1 --inspect embedding```

maria-dev: ran that — embedding matrix shape is (50265, 1536) so checkpoint matches tokenizer. Weird, so why did runtime read config as 50000?

ritesh-ml: Could be that model/config.json in the tar is an older draft. We have two config sources: model/config.json and runtime/serving_config.yaml — the serving config can override vocab_size for compatibility. Maybe the packer uploaded an older config. Grab the config from the S3 tar and diff.

maria-dev: found config.json inside tar — it is indeed 50000. But a separate config in the manifest.json (uploader metadata) lists 50265. Looks like packaging bug: weights from latest training + tokenizer from latest, but config from previous export.

sara-se: OK path forward: update model/config.json in S3 to match 50265 and bump model_version to v1.1, then re-run validate. Also we should add a preflight check in uploader to fail if embedding.shape[0] != config.vocab_size. I'll open a PR later. :+1:

anya-oncall: FYI when you re-upload, make sure runtime flag gqa_mode is enabled. aurora was trained with GQA (grouped queries) so attention default may not be compatible. Can we also validate attention impl?

tony-runtime: Good catch. For GQA we need config.attention = {type: "gqa", qk_groups: 2} or the runtime will try standard qkv and mis-shape. Also check sliding window settings: aurora uses rolling prefix KV and a sliding window of 2048 with chunked kv; if serving_config.max_seq_len < 4096 we need rope scaling.

maria-dev: what's the recommended rope scaling param? we saw some hallucinations at long context in evals.

ritesh-ml: For this model we used linear RoPE scaling with base=2048 and factor=1.5 for long contexts. In config: ```"rope_scaling": {"type": "linear", "base": 2048, "factor": 1.5}``` Runtime expects either "linear" or "dynamic" keys. If missing, it defaults to none and long-context behavior will degrade.

sara-se: Also note our unified runtime has two attention kernels: flash_attn (fast, no rope-scaling) and compat_attn (slower, supports rope_scaling/gqa). Packaging should include a manifest entry so router can pick compat_attn if rope_scaling/GQA present. Add to serving_config.yaml: ```kernels_preferred: [compat_attn, flash_attn]``` then runtime will try compat first.

maria-dev: I've patched config.json (v1.1) and added rope_scaling + attention.gqa in serving_config.yaml. Uploaded to s3 and re-run `python tools/validate_model.py --s3 s3://redwood-models/aurora/13b/mqa/v1.1`. Coming back with a new error: ```RuntimeError: sliding_window.chunk_size (512) incompatible with context_window 2048 for MQA grouping```.

tony-runtime: That means the sliding window chunk must be divisible by group_size for MQA. For aurora group_size is 4 (MQA=Grouped Attention ratio). Set sliding_window.chunk_size to 256 or 1024 depending on latency tradeoff. I vote 256 for lower mem pressure.

maria-dev: Switched chunk_size to 256, revalidated — all good now. validate script outputs: ```VALIDATION PASSED: tokenizer/config/weights/attention/rope_scaling/kernels``` :rocket:

deploy-bot: deploy request queued for aurora-13b-mqa v1.1 -> dedicated-pool-canary. ETA canary start in 10m.

anya-oncall: I'll monitor canary for latency and token-level quality regressions. @sara-se please keep an eye on cost delta from MQA changes.

sara-se: Will do. Also opened PR #2485 to add the uploader preflight checks + manifest kernel hint. @tony-runtime @ritesh-ml please review when you have cycles.

tony-runtime: Reviewing now. If green, we can merge and mark onboard complete. :eyes: 

maria-dev: Thanks everyone — ping me if canary flakes.
